title: Privileged Moments
coreMove: Spot the short window when a question has made the right identity available for the real request.
sourcePressure: The source defines privileged moments as points when people are unusually receptive because the right self-relevant idea is active, including pre-questions about helpful or adventurous identity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Any good timing or emotional mood is a privileged moment.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator asking shoppers to register at the end of lunch hour
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether people see themselves as helpers before hearing the time cost
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator asks passersby to check a card naming a helpful act they did this week before showing the donation signup slot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding table outside a grocery entrance with red appointment cards

exampleSpecs.audience: a clerk offering first-time hikers a harder route option
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether caution or adventurous identity is active when choosing the trail
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the clerk asks which past trip made them feel bold before unfolding the route map
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp trail map spread under a plexiglass counter

exampleSpecs.audience: a librarian seeking weekend shelving help from regular patrons
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether patrons answer as busy customers or as people who keep the library running
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the librarian asks what shelf they always check first before pointing to the volunteer calendar for that section
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a patron holding a mystery novel near a half-empty shelf

exampleSpecs.audience: a product manager inviting users to test a risky feature
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether users feel like careful critics before the beta request
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the invite begins with a one-click question about the last bug they caught, then reveals the beta slot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a release-notes panel with one highlighted bug report

exampleSpecs.audience: a block captain asking residents to store sandbags
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether residents see themselves as prepared neighbors before hearing the chore
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain asks residents to name who checked on them during the last storm before offering the sandbag signup
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a porch rail wet from afternoon rain

exampleSpecs.audience: a registrar asking families to join a mentor program
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether parents answer as overbooked adults or guardians of beginners
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the registrar asks parents to write the first instrument someone helped them learn before handing over the mentor card
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a violin case open on a hallway bench

skillTargets: recognize when a self-image has become active
design a pre-question that makes a relevant identity salient
avoid mistaking convenience timing for a privileged moment
transfer the idea to donation, beta, safety, and volunteer choices

tryThisNowSpec: Write one pre-question that makes a relevant identity active before a real request, then remove any wording that flatters, traps, or pressures the person.
